worksheet.title: Plan and Code
worksheet.subtitle: Plan it, write it, run it, change it
worksheet.learning_goal: I can plan and write code to reach a goal, then change it for a new goal.

parts.title: You are the coder
parts.text: Now you plan the whole code. Fill the empty move blocks so Bit reaches the goal ★. Plan it, write the blocks, predict the landing, then run it to check. Forward adds; back takes away.

parts.title: Goal 1 — start at 1, reach 5
parts.note: Fill the two move blocks to reach 5.

parts.title: Plan and run
parts.prompt: Fill the 2 empty blocks so Bit goes from 1 to 5. PREDICT the landing, then run to check. Write the blocks you used.

parts.title: Goal 2 — start at 2, reach 3 (challenge)
parts.note: Use ONE forward block and ONE back block.

parts.title: Challenge
parts.prompt: Fill the 2 empty blocks so Bit goes from 2 to 3, using one forward block and one back block. Run it to check. Write what you used.

parts.title: You try — change your code
parts.prompt: Take your Goal 1 code (it reaches 5). Change ONE block so Bit lands on 4 instead. What did you change, and where does Bit land now?

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: A coder plans the steps, writes the code, runs it to test, and changes it when the goal changes. You can read code, write code, fix code, and change code — you are a coder!

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: The unit finale: students plan and write a full set of instructions to a goal, meet a harder goal that mixes forward and back, then change their instructions for a new goal. Read, write, fix, and change code — all in one page. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: Paper and pencil only. Optional: a floor number line 0 to 5 with a star on 5, plus move cards, so students can lay out and test their plan before writing it.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 20–25 minutes)
text: 1. Show them first (you do). Model Goal 1 — count from 1 to 5 (4 steps forward) and split it: "forward 2, forward 2." Run it to land on 5.
2. Do one together (we do). Exercise 1: students plan their own blocks to reach 5, predict, then run. Exercise 2 (challenge): from 2 to 3 using one forward and one back (e.g. forward 2, back 1).
3. Let them try alone (you do). Exercise 3: change one block of the Goal 1 code so Bit reaches 4 (e.g. last forward 2 → forward 1).
4. Celebrate: "You can read, write, fix, and change code — that is what coders do."

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — start 1 → 5: any two forward blocks that total 4, e.g. forward 2, forward 2 (or forward 1, forward 3).
Exercise 2 — start 2 → 3 with one forward + one back: e.g. forward 2, back 1 (2 → 4 → 3). The pair must net +1.
Exercise 3 — change the last forward 2 to forward 1: 1 → 3 → 4. Bit lands on 4, one less, because the last step is now one smaller.
Why it works: the start sets the number and the moves run in order; plan the total change (forward adds, back subtracts) to match the distance to the goal.

parts.title: If students get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for (Ex 2): using two forward or two back blocks. Re-read "one forward AND one back" and have them net +1 from 2 to 3.
Make it easier: allow a single move block for Goal 1 (forward 4).
Make it harder: ask for a second, different answer for Goal 1, or a plan that reaches 5 from start 0.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum link (official wording)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential events.
In plain terms: students follow (or write) step-by-step instructions, in order, to get a result.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.
In plain terms: students read instructions someone wrote, change one, and explain what the change did.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The student writes working instructions for each goal and correctly changes the Goal 1 code to land on 4.
